newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks give up gains after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks give up gains after U.S. data.

text.p: Norwegian shares continued in reverse on Tuesday after a marginal early uptrend was wiped out by a spate of U.S. indicators.
Dealers said activity was low and an early recovery in Norsk Hydro and food and beverage-based conglomerate Orkla were unable to support the market.
Oslo's Total share index slipped 0.19 percent to 1,173.58 points in dull turnover of 569 million crowns.
Norsk Hydro struggled to recover from a 4.50 crown fall a day earlier as dealers reviewed reports of tough compeition in the European fertilisers market.

The share relinquished all gains near the close after Hydro put out a statement saying that Aker Maritime was claiming one billion crowns above the agreed contract price for the Njord oil platform. Hydro closed 0.50 crowns down at 381 crown in turnover of 102 million crowns.
Orkla recovered recent lost ground, gaining six crowns in the A share and 7.50 crowns in the B's to end at 552 and 504.50 crowns respectively.
"Orkla's had a rough time since the results, but people are revaluing the company and realising it is not such a poor stock. There's a lot of good value in the company," said a broker.
